newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Delta CEO to rebalance cost effort.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Delta CEO to rebalance cost effort.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Chief Executive Leo Mullin on Friday said he would seek greater balance in the airline's approach to cost controls while trying to improve its customer service.

"When any organization has such a relentless attention to cost ... sometimes the balance can get out of whack. And my hypothesis would be that that's what's happened here and we just bring it back a little," he told Reuters.
"At the same time, we have to continue to pay attention to efficiency because it's the equation of customer satisfaction and efficiency that yields maximum shareholder value."
"The best companies in America do it all the time. There's example after example. It is a total misconception to think that you cannot do both," he added.

Mullin was speaking after being named president and chief executive of Delta. He replaced Ron Allen, who resigned as chief executive on July 31 after a dispute with board members, including Gerald Grinstein, who was named chairman.
